Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford Win Nobel Prize in Economics

Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford have been awarded the 2026 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences by the Royal Swedish Academy. The prize recognizes their work on the microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilization, specifically their contributions to understanding how monetary and fiscal policy can help manage economic fluctuations, smooth boom-and-bust cycles, and assist governments and central banks in managing economic instability. Their insights are noted to have better equipped policymakers to deal with economic shocks, aiming to limit unemployment and inflation. The award comes with a prize of 12 million Swedish crowns, approximately $1.2 million.
